_comment: CASE 3A -- PARTIAL PARTICIPATION, MILP (single-path) leg. Same NIC-per-GPU topology, same active set [0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], same clock and same objective as mini_2gpu_2nic_alltoall_partial_3A.json, solved with the chunk-level MILP (formulation 1) at num_chunks 1: each (src, dst) pair owns exactly ONE indivisible 1 GB chunk that traverses exactly ONE path end to end. The solver still picks the BEST single-path assignment, so LP-minus-MILP is a LOWER bound on what per-pair multipath is worth.
_known_limitation: KNOWN LIMITATION, DOES NOT TRIGGER HERE. The MILP under-charges delivery time on a cut-through path when a link is too slow to clock a whole chunk out in one epoch: it pays the store-and-forward cost (1 epoch + beta) once at the first GPU->switch hop and charges later fabric hops only propagation delay, so it credits 1 + beta(FIRST hop) instead of the correct 1 + max(beta over the legs used) = ceil(chunk / min bandwidth along the path). This topology's links are UNIFORM -- 100Gbps GPU NICs and 100Gbps leaf-spine uplinks -- and the epoch is one chunk on a 100Gbps link, so every link's epoch_capacity is exactly 1 chunk, beta is 0 everywhere, and the under-charge has nothing to bite on. Verified for this file. The non-uniform partners (cases 1A, 2B, 2C on the 50Gbps-uplink topologies) DO hit it at their pinned 0.08 s epoch and say so in their own _known_limitation; the reported makespan here is trustworthy, theirs is not.
_participation: active GPUs [0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]; passive GPUs [1, 7]. Node map: 0/1 = srv0.gpu0/gpu1, 2/3 = srv1, 4/5 = srv2, 6/7 = srv3; 8-11 = the per-host hsw; 12/13 = leaf0/leaf1; 14/15 = spine0/spine1. srv0+srv1 on leaf0, srv2+srv3 on leaf1, so participation is 3-and-3 across the leaves and 1/2/2/1 across the hosts. Each GPU owns its own 100Gbps NIC, so a passive GPU is a relay WITH BANDWIDTH -- unlike the shared-NIC case 2C. num_chunks 1 = one chunk per (src, dst) PAIR, and the chunk axis is widened by the ACTIVE count, giving 30 chunks of 1 GB.
_vs_lp: Differences from mini_2gpu_2nic_alltoall_partial_3A.json, and only these: formulation 1 (MILP) not 2 (LP); symmetry false not true; num_epochs 10 not 12; distinct log_file and schedule_output_file. Held fixed: topo_file, passive_node_indices, chunk_size 1, collective 2, num_chunks 1, switch_copy false, epoch_type 2 / epoch_duration -1 (both resolve to 0.08 s), switch_pipeline true, solution_method 1, time_limit 5. ALSO DIFFERENT: objective_type 2 (TOTAL_DEMAND) here against the LP's 6 (LEXICOGRAPHIC) -- so the difference is integrality PLUS objective, not integrality alone; it is still not granularity. See _objective_note for exactly what that trades.
_objective_note: OBJECTIVE: TOTAL_DEMAND (objective_type 2), NOT the lexicographic 6 the LP partner uses. WHAT IT IS: allgather.py::objective_formulation builds -100 * sum_k max(sum_(s,d,c) total_demand_sat[s][d][c][k] - (Demand - 1), 0). The inner term is 1 exactly when EVERY demand is already satisfied by the end of epoch k and 0 otherwise, so the objective pays 100 per epoch of the horizon that the collective has already finished in -- i.e. it MINIMIZES THE COMPLETION EPOCH directly. That is the point of using it here: '3-Epochs_Required' becomes the quantity the solver is actually optimizing, so a reported makespan can be compared against the analytic bound as a real optimality claim rather than as an artifact of where a latency-sum objective happened to leave the last straggler. WHAT IT GIVES UP -- read this before judging the routing: objective_type 6 carried two lower-priority tiers that 2 does not have. Tier 2 penalized HOST RELAY (volume a GPU forwards on behalf of another GPU) and tier 3 penalized SWITCH-CHAIN LENGTH (flow entering a switch: 0 for a direct link, 1 for gpu->switch->gpu, 3 for a leaf->spine->leaf detour). Under objective 2 the solver is INDIFFERENT among all schedules that finish in the same epoch, so expect gratuitous relays and spine detours that carry no cost -- the schedule stays correct and makespan-optimal, but it is no longer the tidiest routing that achieves that makespan, and a relay or a long chain in the output is no longer evidence that it was needed. MIDDLE GROUND if that matters: objective_type 5 (TOTAL_DEMAND_MIN_SWITCH_HOPS) is this same completion reward plus a GAMMA=1e-4 per-unit penalty on switch->switch flow, small enough never to trade completion time for hops, which restores a shortest-chain preference (but still no relay tier). COST: the objective adds two continuous aux vars and one max_ general constraint per epoch, which is negligible next to the (source, link, chunk, epoch) flow variables. COMPARABILITY CAVEAT: the LP partner still uses objective_type 6, so the LP-vs-MILP difference is no longer integrality ALONE -- it is integrality plus objective. For the makespan that is fine (both are measured against the same analytic lower bound, which neither objective can beat); for a ROUTING diff, remember the LP is tie-broken toward fewer relays and shorter switch chains and this MILP is not.
_why_symmetry_off: Orbit averaging is free on the LP (convex feasible set, so the symmetric average of an optimum is an optimum) but a REAL restriction on the integral problem, where an equal count across an orbit need not exist at the integral optimum. Cutting off that optimum is the measurement error this file exists to avoid.
_expected: T* = 0.4 s = 5 epochs -- a TIE with the LP on this clock, and for the same reason as 2C: the cut needs 9 chunks per direction, a 100Gbps uplink carries exactly 1 chunk per 0.08 s epoch, 2 uplinks give 2 per epoch, so ceil(9/2) = 5 epochs with or without splitting. gpu0's and gpu6's own NICs land on the same number by coincidence -- 5 chunks at 1 chunk per epoch = 5 epochs -- which is why a schedule that never relays through the passive twins can still reach 5; that figure is not an independent bound, since each lone active GPU can borrow its passive twin's idle NIC through hsw (see the LP file's _expected). The LP's continuous 4.5-epoch cut bound is not a legal answer for either one: the makespan is an integer number of epochs, so that half epoch is the ceiling, not integrality. WHAT TO COMPARE WHEN THE MAKESPANS TIE: diff the '30-Chunk paths' sections -- every MILP demand lists ONE path, the LP's 18 cross-leaf demands should be fanned across both spines -- and check that both keep each middle host's intra-host pair (2<->3, 4<->5) on hsw rather than out through a NIC, and note that a detour through passive gpu1/gpu7 is NOT suppressed here: at 5 epochs the relay is unnecessary, but objective_type 2 has no relay tier, so one may appear at no cost. The LP partner does relay through the passive twins for a latency reason (see the LP file's _expected); this leg may relay for no reason at all. TO SEE A REAL GAP, run the LP at epoch_duration 0.04, where it reaches 0.36 s = 9 epochs and MUST relay 0.5 GB of gpu0's traffic through passive gpu1's NIC; this formulation must not be quoted for timing there: halving the epoch forfeits the uniform-bandwidth immunity this file relies on (every link drops to 0.5 chunks per epoch, beta becomes 1) and the cut-through under-charge in _known_limitation starts to bite. Its ROUTING at 0.04 s is still worth diffing; its clock is not.
_epoch_note: epoch_type 2 (SLOWEST_LINK), epoch_duration -1 -> 0.08 s = 1 GB / 12.5 GB/s, the 100Gbps NIC, which is also the uplink rate on this variant. Inherited verbatim from the LP file so the pair shares one clock. A finer epoch is a FLOOR for this formulation, and not because it is rejected -- it is accepted and silently mis-timed. Below one chunk per epoch on a link, beta = ceil(1/epoch_capacity) - 1 > 0 turns that link's capacity row into a (beta+1)-epoch sliding window, which charges the chunk's transmission RATE but not its LATENCY: the cut-through switch->GPU arrival term in node_constraint_helper drops beta, so the solve comes back optimistically fast rather than infeasible (measured on case 1A: 0.08 s reported against a 0.16 s per-link transmission time, vs 0.48 s for the same run with switch_pipeline false). Keep the clock at or above one chunk's worth of the narrowest link a chunk must cross, where beta == 0 and the window row is the exact per-epoch row; verified for this file -- every link's epoch_capacity is >= 1 chunk.
_horizon_note: num_epochs is the MILP's time horizon and it costs -- one integer flow variable per (source, link, chunk, epoch), and with 30 chunks on 16 nodes that product is the whole model size, so 10 against a 5-epoch bound is deliberately only 2x. If the solve comes back INFEASIBLE rather than merely slow, raise this first; if it comes back slow, raise time_limit or drop to solution_method 2. With objective_type 2 the horizon no longer DISTORTS the answer, only the model size: the reward is paid per epoch in which the whole collective is already complete, so a larger num_epochs just widens the reward range and the solver still drives the completion epoch down. Contrast objective_type 6, under which the reported makespan was only an upper bound (its tier 1 minimizes the SUM of completion epochs, not the max, so a straggler could drift late inside a generous horizon) -- see _objective_note.
_hierarchical_note: hierarchical is false here and a hierarchical run is not a substitute for this file in any case: the hierarchical path is LP-only downstream (the stitch emits LP-format schedules). This is the single-path GROUND TRUTH at 16 fine nodes for this active set.
_topology_note: The topology comes from the .topo DSL file; topo_file SELECTS it, so TECCLSolver.get_topology builds a DslTopology and `name` is only the free-form label for output filenames and the Gurobi log. The path is relative to the repo root.
